question: What is the primary anatomical location where cervical cancer typically originates?
explanation: Cervical cancer primarily develops in the transformation zone, where the endocervical and ectocervical cell types meet and undergo active cellular turnover. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h1)

question: Why is cervical cancer considered a significant public health concern in Nigeria?

options.A: Rapid metastatic spread prior to primary infection
options.B: Strict federal bans on prophylactic vaccines
options.C: Limited access to routine screening infrastructure
options.D: High rates of spontaneous genetic mutations in the population

explanation: Resource-constrained settings often lack widespread, accessible screening programs, leading to delayed diagnoses at advanced stages of the disease. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h1)

question: Which specific viral strains are most commonly responsible for high-risk cervical cancer development?
explanation: High-risk strains HPV 16 and 18 account for the majority of invasive cervical carcinomas worldwide. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h2)

question: How does HIV co-infection directly impact the natural history of HPV in the cervix?

options.A: It neutralizes the inflammatory response required for tumor growth
options.B: It impairs immune-mediated viral clearance, promoting persistence
options.C: It accelerates the immediate shedding of healthy squamous cells
options.D: It converts high-risk viral strains into benign epithelial warts

explanation: Compromised cell-mediated immunity in HIV-positive individuals prevents the body from clearing viral loads, drastically raising the risk of persistent infection. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h2)

question: What is the primary function of the HPV E6 oncoprotein within infected host cells?

options.A: Enhances basement membrane stability against invasion
options.B: Stimulates the direct production of protective antibodies
options.C: Inactivates the retinoblastoma protein to halt mitosis
options.D: Promotes the degradation of the p53 tumor suppressor protein

explanation: The E6 oncoprotein targets p53 for destruction, preventing damaged cells from undergoing programmed cell death and allowing mutations to accumulate. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h3)

question: What pathological finding defines the progression from cervical intraepithelial neoplasia to invasive cancer?

options.A: Inflammatory necrosis of the ectocervical surface
options.B: Breaching of the epithelial basement membrane
options.C: Complete clearance of the viral genome from basal cells
options.D: Transformation of squamous cells into glandular tissue

explanation: Invasive cancer occurs only when abnormal cells break through the basement membrane and invade the underlying stromal tissues. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h3)

question: What is the most characteristic early symptom of cervical cancer?
explanation: Post-coital or intermenstrual bleeding is typically the first physical warning sign prompting clinical evaluation for cervical pathology. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h4)

question: A patient with advanced cervical cancer presents with unilateral leg swelling and back pain. What pathophysiological mechanism best explains this finding?

options.A: Metastatic bone lesions settling exclusively in the femur
options.B: Acute inflammatory reaction following routine biopsy
options.C: Systemic cachexia leading to generalized third-spacing
options.D: Tumor compression of pelvic wall structures and nerve plexuses

explanation: Advanced pelvic tumor extension can obstruct venous and lymphatic drainage causing leg edema, while nerve compression leads to referred back and pelvic pain. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h4)

question: What visual change occurs when acetic acid is applied to abnormal cervical tissue during a VIA screening?

options.A: The tissue turns an acetowhite color
options.B: The lesion develops bright yellow ulcerations
options.D: The affected area produces active bleeding

explanation: Abnormal cellular changes have higher nuclear protein concentrations that coagulate and reflect light as a distinct acetowhite patch upon acid application. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h5)

question: A community health nurse in a rural clinic uses a screen-and-treat protocol with VIA. What is the primary advantage of this operational approach?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any physical examination of the cervix
options.B: It provides definitive histological confirmation of invasive carcinoma
options.C: It completely replaces the need for HPV vaccination in young girls
options.D: It minimizes loss to follow-up by providing same-day treatment for positive results

explanation: In rural settings, patients often fail to return for delayed lab results; treating immediately upon a positive visual inspection drastically improves clinical compliance. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of performing a colposcopy after an abnormal Pap smear?

options.A: To magnify and closely inspect the cervix for biopsy targeting
options.B: To destroy all superficial pathogens causing vaginal discharge
options.C: To administer localized radiation therapy to the tumor bed
options.D: To measure systemic hormone levels driving cell growth

explanation: Colposcopy uses magnification and staining agents to locate abnormal vascular and epithelial patterns so the clinician can take targeted punch biopsies. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h6)

question: Why is Lugol's iodine solution applied to the cervix during diagnostic evaluations?

options.A: It acts as a potent local anesthetic to numb the cervical stroma before biopsy
options.B: It permanently sterilizes the transformation zone against recurring viral loads
options.C: Healthy glycogen-rich cells take up the brown stain, while abnormal cells remain unstained
options.D: It stimulates immediate regression of high-grade intraepithelial lesions

explanation: Normal mature squamous cells contain abundant glycogen which stains brown with iodine, whereas dysplastic or malignant cells lack glycogen and appear pale or yellow (Schiller-positive). [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h6)

question: What is the standard primary treatment approach for locally advanced cervical cancer?
explanation: Locally advanced lesions respond best to a combined regimen of external/internal radiation alongside sensitizing chemotherapy rather than surgery alone. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h7)

question: What role does cisplatin typically serve when administered alongside radiotherapy in cervical cancer management?

options.A: It completely prevents local tissue fibrosis caused by radiation beams
options.B: It suppresses systemic bone marrow activity to stop white blood cell growth
options.C: It replaces the need for surgical removal of pelvic lymph nodes
options.D: It acts as a radiosensitizer to make cancer cells more vulnerable to radiation

explanation: Cisplatin is administered concurrently in low doses to sensitize tumor cells to the cytotoxic effects of ionizing radiation, improving local control rates. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h7)

question: A patient undergoing pelvic radiation therapy for cervical cancer reports burning urination and frequent urgency. What nursing assessment is most appropriate?

options.A: Advise the patient to completely stop drinking all fluids to rest the bladder
options.B: Prepare the patient immediately for emergency surgical closure of a fistula
options.C: Monitor for signs of radiation-induced cystitis and urinary tract irritation
options.D: Check for signs of acute metastatic spread to the cerebral cortex

explanation: Radiation to pelvic fields commonly irritates the bladder mucosa, resulting in inflammatory symptoms resembling a urinary tract infection known as radiation cystitis. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h8)

question: What is a primary focus when delivering palliative nursing care to a patient with terminal cervical cancer?

options.A: Focusing solely on routine preventative screening for secondary malignancies
options.B: Enforcing strict bedrest with complete isolation from family members
options.C: Optimizing comfort, pain management, and holistic family support
options.D: Aggressively titrating high-dose chemotherapeutic agents to achieve remission

explanation: Palliative nursing shifts the goal from curative treatment to symptom control, pain relief, and emotional support to ensure quality of life at the end of life. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h8)

question: At what age group are prophylactic HPV vaccination programs primarily targeted for maximum clinical effectiveness?

options.A: Infants immediately following routine neonatal immunizations
options.B: Adolescent girls aged 9 to 14 years before sexual debut
options.C: Adult women over the age of 50 during routine menopause clinics
options.D: Pregnant women during their second trimester antenatal visits

explanation: Vaccines generate the highest antibody response and protect best when given prior to any potential exposure to the human papillomavirus through sexual contact. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h9)

question: Why is the combination of HPV vaccination and routine screening considered the ultimate dual-layered defense against cervical cancer?

options.A: Screening eliminates the need for any follow-up care if the vaccine was administered
options.B: Vaccination prevents new infections, while screening catches pre-existing or breakthrough lesions early
options.C: Vaccination neutralizes all known non-viral forms of gynecological malignancies
options.D: Vaccination cures active invasive tumors, while screening repairs damaged vaginal tissue

explanation: Prophylactic vaccines stop future infections from targeted strains, but screening remains necessary to catch abnormalities caused by non-vaccine strains or pre-existing infections. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h9)
